metadata.title: Awesome Tactile Hands
metadata.scope: Public datasets that record touch across the hand during manipulation: human tactile gloves and dexterous robot hands with tactile sensing.

datasets.name: TouchScale
datasets.title: TouchScale: 500 Hours of Human Vision and Touch for Visual-Tactile Learning
datasets.summary: Bimanual tactile gloves with 880 taxels per hand, recorded with head-mounted RGB-D and two wrist cameras across about 2K everyday tasks.
datasets.hand: Tachin glove (commercial)

sensor.note: Normal pressure, 1.5 x 1.5 mm cells, 15 pads over five fingers and palm (palmar side), spatial resolution below 2 mm. Hardware spec 50 Hz WiFi / 100 Hz USB; released data is 35-90 Hz, timestamped per sample. Release NPZ also carries tangential (shear) components per pad.

scale.text: 500 h, ~87K episodes, ~2K tasks, 1.5K+ objects, ~20 participants, 9 collection settings (800+ scene configurations)

datasets.access: Gated on Hugging Face. 100 h / 15,324 episodes / 929 tasks (~1.08 TB) released so far; the rest is planned before November 2026.
caveats: No hand-pose capture; the paper estimates pose with WiLoR.

cameras.resolution: 1280x720 RGB; depth 640x480 native (released registered to RGB at 1280x720)

tracking.note: Paper runs WiLoR on auto-detected hand crops for its experiments; no pose file in the release file list and no hand-tracking hardware.

unconfirmed: Glove maker not named; paper calls it the 'Tachin Glove' (product name only). Data were captured by vendor Noitom for Overfit Lab.
Transduction principle not stated (paper: 'flexible tactile sensing gloves', normal pressure).
scenes=9 is the paper's 'high-level collection settings' for the full 500 h; the 100 h HF release lists 22 finer scene types. scene_types are the 7 environments the paper names (of 9).
subjects: paper says ~20; the 100 h release card says 24 pseudonymous participants.
Release status: 100 h / 15,324 episodes / 929 tasks / 905+ objects on HF; 500 h planned before Nov 2026.
Paper says the glove records normal pressure only, but the release NPZ includes tf_tactile_x/y 'tangential components'.
Depth resolution: paper 640x480; card says depth_head.mkv is 1280x720 registered to head RGB.

datasets.name: EgoTouch
datasets.title: TouchAnything: A Dataset and Framework for Bimanual Tactile Estimation from Egocentric Video
datasets.summary: Bimanual pressure gloves with Rokoko finger tracking and Vive wrist trackers, a chest camera and two fisheye wrist cameras, 208 tasks in 5 kinds of scenes.
datasets.hand: Custom pressure gloves + Rokoko mocap gloves

sensor.note: 256 raw channels per hand; the release code maps 138 (left) / 147 (right) of them, of which 15 / 24 are finger bend sensors, leaving about 123 pressure taxels per hand. Remapped to a hand-shaped 21 x 21 grid; the glove also streams an IMU quaternion.

scale.text: ~20 h, 1,891 episodes, 208 tasks, 1,000+ objects, ~2.1M frames, 5 scene types

datasets.access: Hugging Face, 88.5 GB.
caveats: The paper reports 256 channels per glove; part of them are bend sensors, so the pressure taxel count (about 123) is derived from the release code.
Release counts differ from the paper: 1,933 episodes / 213 tasks on Hugging Face against 1,891 / 208 in the paper.

tracking.note: 21 joints per hand, transformed into the Vive frame via the wrist tracker when calibrated (rokoko_hands.json).
Three trackers (chest, left_wrist, right_wrist) via OpenXR; 7-D poses in vive_poses.json.
Release also ships wilor_hands.json (1,930 episodes) and hamer_hands.json (1,536 episodes).

other: finger bend sensors in the glove stream

sources: local: ~/data/ext/egotouch (episode files, split.json; ffprobe of chest/left/right.mp4)
unconfirmed: Camera models not stated. Egocentric camera is called head-mounted in the main text but 'chest/head-mounted' in the appendix; files are chest.mp4 and the Vive role is 'chest'. README calls it a 'wide-angle' camera.

taxels_per_hand=256 is the raw channel count. The released mapping (pressure_position_mapping_*.json) uses 138 (L) / 147 (R) unique channels; configs/hand_joint_positions.json marks 15 (L) / 24 (R) of them as finger bend sensors, leaving ~123 (L) / ~129 (R) pressure channels.
Glove maker not named ('custom pressure-sensing gloves'); raw file is named jq_pressure.json, which suggests but does not establish a JQ Industries glove.
Release counts differ from the paper: HF lists 1,933 episode folders / 213 tasks; local split.json lists 2,228 episodes / 228 tasks; paper and README say 1,891 / 208.
Number of participants not stated.
scenes/scene_types from the paper's five environment categories, confirmed by the release's top-level folders (Home/Office/Outdoor/Retail/Workbench).
taxels per hand (123) derived from the release's channel mapping, not stated in the paper
Glove maker from a figure on the TouchAnything project page labelled 'JQ-Industries Fabric Tactile Glove'; the paper text says custom pressure gloves.

datasets.name: TactiDex
datasets.title: TactiDex: A Real-World Tactile-Guided Benchmark for Human-Like Dexterous Manipulation
datasets.summary: Piezoresistive glove over a MANUS mocap glove with OptiTrack object tracking, single-hand and bimanual, retargeted to Inspire hands.
datasets.hand: Piezoresistive glove over MANUS Metagloves Pro

sensor.note: 162 elements per glove on fingertips and palm, worn over a MANUS mocap glove; force resolution up to 0.01 N.

scale.text: 757 sequences, 49 objects, 10 subjects, 5.1M frames, single mocap workspace

datasets.access: No data or code link on the project page or arXiv as of 2026-10-15.
caveats: No RGB video: pose comes from the MANUS gloves and OptiTrack.

tracking.note: Paper: IMU measurements fused with optical tracking data; MANO fitted to the keypoints by L-BFGS.
Rigid marker backplate on the Metaglove; 1.2 m x 1.8 m workspace; eSync hardware sync.
49 scanned object meshes registered in the OptiTrack frame.

unconfirmed: hours=11.8 derived from 5.1M frames (Table 1) at the 120 Hz kinematic/pose rate; the paper states no duration, and the frame count could be counted differently (e.g. per hand).
Number of distinct tasks not stated (only single-hand vs bimanual and action types in a Sankey figure).
No RGB/egocentric video is described as part of the dataset.
Tactile glove maker/model not named.
scenes=1: all capture is in one OptiTrack workspace (lab).
Project page shows Code/Data as 'Coming Soon'.

datasets.name: T-Rex
datasets.title: T-Rex: Tactile-Reactive Dexterous Manipulation
datasets.summary: Bimanual teleoperation on two 22-DoF Sharpa Wave hands with five fingertip tactile sensors each, in LeRobot format.
datasets.hand: Sharpa Wave (22 DoF) x 2 on Dexmate Vega-1

sensor.note: Five fingertip sensors per hand (Sharpa Wave built-in). Per sensor: raw sensor image (320x240 grayscale), estimated deformation map (240x240 grayscale), estimated 6-axis net wrench. Recorded at 30 Hz with the teleop loop. No palm sensing.

scale.text: Released: ~50 h, 5,464 episodes, 5.47M frames @30 fps, 22 motor primitives x 207 objects (paper: 100 h, 7,755 episodes, 502 object-primitive pairs)

datasets.access: Hugging Face, ungated, 1.53 TB, LeRobot v3.
caveats: Fingertips only.

cameras.model: Stereolabs ZED X Mini (left RGB stream only)

tracking.note: observation.state = 2x(7 arm + 22 hand) joint positions; action = joint targets at 30 Hz
paper also lists SE(3) end-effector poses per episode
fingertip positions retargeted to Sharpa Wave via Sharpa's diff-IK (Pinocchio + CasADi)
SE(3) wrist targets -> arm diff-IK (Pink)

other: raw + deformation tactile videos (20 streams, lossless)

unconfirmed: Sensing principle set to optical (camera-based) from the released raw sensor images, which show a camera view of a patterned elastomer; the paper, card and code do not name the principle.
hours=50 is the dataset card's figure (5,473,459 frames / 30 fps = 50.7 h); paper Appendix G says 100 h and 7,755 episodes - the public release is about half of the paper's dataset.
tasks=22 counts motor primitives; the card's total_tasks=5,370 counts unique language captions.
scenes=6 = 'six distinct tabletop backdrops' (App. G); collected in a controlled lab, so scene_types left empty.
Head ZED X Mini is a stereo camera but only its left monocular RGB stream is recorded.

datasets.name: OpenTouch
datasets.title: OpenTouch: Bringing Full-Hand Touch to Real-World Interaction
datasets.summary: In-the-wild right-hand pressure glove with Meta Aria egocentric video, Rokoko hand pose and text labels across 14 environments.
datasets.hand: Piezoresistive film glove + Rokoko

sensor.note: FPC-routed 16 x 16 electrode grid around a commercial piezoresistive film, 169 taxels on the palmar side; normal pressure only; ESP-NOW wireless.

scale.text: 5.1 h recorded, 2,900 annotated clips (3 h), ~800 object types, 14 environments, 29 grasp types

datasets.access: Google Drive, via scripts/download_data.sh in the code repo.
caveats: Right hand only.

cameras.model: Meta Project Aria glasses (RGB POV camera, 110 deg FOV)

tracking.note: IMU + EMF sensor fusion, seven 6-DoF sensors per glove, 30 Hz; right hand only. Release HDF5 has right_hand_landmarks (21x3), right_wrist_pos, right_palm_pos.

other: Aria camera poses per frame (camera_poses in release HDF5)
GPT-5 clip labels: object, object category, environment, action, grasp type, description

sources: local: ~/data/ext/opentouch (repo README, scripts/download_data.sh, ann/final_annotations/*.csv, dl/*.hdf5) -- read only
unconfirmed: objects: paper text and project page say 'over 8,000 objects from 14 categories', but the paper's Table 1 says ~800 object types; the released annotations have 2,038 distinct object names and 110 category labels.
Number of participants not stated.
tasks left null: free exploration, no predefined task list; annotations carry 66 distinct action labels and 29 GRASP-taxonomy grasp types.

scene_types derived from release file prefixes (eat_mcdonalds, eat_ygf, fablab_ml, grocery_plant/target/tj, hardware_homedepot, home_bedroom/kitchen, office_csail/ml, sports_dicks): 12 distinct locations in the local copy vs 14 environments in the paper.
Local annotation CSVs contain 2,958 clips totalling 3.0 h (paper: 2,900 clips, 3 h).
Aria SLAM cameras and IMU were recorded (profile 28) but only RGB appears in the release HDF5.
Paper is ambiguous on finger coverage: 'uniformly cover the fingers and palmar surface'.

datasets.name: EgoTactile
datasets.title: EgoTactile: Learning Grasp Pressure for Everyday Objects from Egocentric Video
datasets.summary: Full-hand 162-sensor pressure glove with egocentric video of grasps on 63 everyday objects, plus a bare-hand test set.
datasets.hand: 162-sensor pressure glove

sensor.note: 162-sensor glove (raw 256-channel vector), 0-350 N; resampled with sample-and-hold to a 15 Hz synchronized timeline. Layout per the code: 4x3 block per fingertip, a 6-sensor group on each finger's middle/proximal segments (averaged), and the palm.

scale.text: 5.82 h, 768 gloved-hand clips (+75 bare-hand clips, 0.61 h), 63 objects in 7 categories, 12 participants, green-screen lab

datasets.access: Hugging Face, 5.48 GB.
caveats: Grasping everyday objects rather than dexterous manipulation.
No hand pose.
Video is released at 15 fps; 692 gloved clips (11 subjects) are on Hugging Face so far, against 768 in the paper.

other: object metadata (name, category, weight, material, fill state)
participant metadata (gender, hand length; paper adds age, weight, body fat)
bare-hand subset with off-camera gloved-hand labels

sources: local: ~/data/ext/egotactile (card README, sample clip data.json + video.mp4)
unconfirmed: Camera captures at 30 fps; released clips are 15 fps (ffprobe and card). Paper uses both head and neck mounts; the card says head-mounted.

Glove maker not named. A co-author is affiliated with JQ Industries (Qingdao), and TactiDex reports a glove with the same spec (162 elements, ~17 Hz) as piezoresistive; neither establishes maker or principle here.

episodes/hours are the paper's gloved-hand totals (768 clips, 5.82 h). The bare-hand set adds 75 clips / 0.61 h. HF currently has 692 gloved clips (11 subjects, 63 objects) and 75 bare-hand clips (3 subjects, 25 objects).
frames=319k from paper Table 1.
Segmentation masks are used as model conditions in the paper but are not listed in the release card.
scenes=1: controlled green-screen lab.

datasets.name: HRDexDB
datasets.title: HRDexDB: A 4D Dexterous Grasping Dataset Across Human and Multiple Robot Embodiments
datasets.summary: Paired human and teleoperated robot grasps (Allegro V5 Plus, Inspire RH56F1 and RH56DFTP, Robotiq 2F-85 on an xArm6) over 100 objects, filmed by a 23-camera rig with MANO hands and object 6D poses; built-in tactile only on the Allegro and Inspire F1 hands.
datasets.hand: Human hand (no tactile); Allegro Hand V5 Plus (16 DoF), Inspire RH56F1, Inspire RH56DFTP, Robotiq 2F-85, each on an xArm6

sensor.note: Robot hands only. Allegro V5 Plus: raw/hand/tactile.npy (T, 4) int32, one value per fingertip sensor, ~99 Hz, 0 to ~1,800 counts. Inspire RH56F1 (right hand): raw/hand/right_tactile.npy, one dict per sample with normal_force, tangential_force and tangential_direction for 8 regions (little, ring, middle, index, thumb, palm_right, palm_middle, palm_left) = 24 scalars at 50 Hz. Inspire RH56DFTP: tactile.npy is empty in all 618 episodes; a per-actuator force.npy (T, 6) at ~50 Hz is present. Robotiq 2F-85: none. Units are not stated. Paper: readings too noisy or sparse to serve as contact labels.
sensor.model: Allegro Hand V5 Plus fingertip tactile sensors; Inspire RH56F1 built-in tactile; Inspire RH56DFTP finger force sensors

scale.text: Release: 2,703 sequences (441 human, 453 Allegro, 592 Inspire F1, 618 Inspire DFTP, 599 Robotiq) over 100 objects, ~14.9 h of synchronized 30 fps capture, 23 views; paper: 3,215 trials (541 human), 43.5M frames (all views)

datasets.access: Hugging Face HRDexDB/HRDexDB, ungated, ~1.56 TB of per-sequence folders (per-camera mp4, raw .npy robot streams, MANO, object pose npz); single files can be fetched; Google Drive ZIP mirror also offered.
caveats: Grasping only: one grasp-and-lift task per sequence; robot trials teleoperated to reproduce a reference human grasp (no frame-level alignment between paired human and robot sequences).
No human tactile; the human hand is a MANO fit from multi-view video.
Inspire RH56DFTP tactile.npy is empty (0 elements) in all 618 released episodes; only a 6-channel force.npy with undocumented units is present, stored as unsigned 16-bit wrap-around (65,535 = -1).
Tactile units, sensor-to-channel mapping and calibration are not documented for any hand; the paper calls the Allegro and Inspire readings too noisy or sparse for contact labels.
Many raw .npy files (arm streams, Inspire F1 hand and tactile, Robotiq hand, teleop) are pickled object arrays and need allow_pickle to load.
Release (2,703 sequences) is smaller than the paper's 3,215 trials; all 453 released Allegro sequences are labelled successful, while the paper reports 52 Allegro failures.
The metadata catalog (metadata/episodes.parquet, 2,104 rows) does not cover the Robotiq sequences; 33 Robotiq folders lack raw/ and 36 lack calibration files.
Videos are 2048x1536 MPEG-4 Part 2 (not H.264), ~230-840 MB per sequence (median, by embodiment) across 22-23 views.

tracking.system: HaMeR 2D keypoints in calibrated views -> triangulation -> MANO fit (shape calibrated by SAM3 silhouettes)
tracking.note: human sequences; per-frame MANO mesh (.obj) and params (.json, incl. 21 joints)

tracking.system: SAM3 masks + FoundPose init + GoTrack multi-view 6D tracking
tracking.note: all embodiments; object_6d_pose_v1/v2 npz, one 4x4 per video frame

tracking.system: robot hand joint states and commands
tracking.note: Allegro, Inspire F1/DFTP, Robotiq
every robot hand is mounted on an xArm6
teleoperation of robot fingers; raw glove skeletons released only for Inspire DFTP and Robotiq sequences
teleoperation of the arm

other: camera intrinsics/extrinsics (+ per-frame ego extrinsics for the helmet)

sources: https://huggingface.co/datasets/HRDexDB/HRDexDB raw files of human/apple/0, allegro_v5/apple/3, inspire_f1/apple/0, inspire_dftp/apple/0, robotiq_2f85/apple/0 and tactile/force files of 9 more robot sequences
unconfirmed: episodes=2,703 counted from sequence folders in the HF tree (human 441, allegro_v5 453, inspire_f1 592, inspire_dftp 618, robotiq_2f85 599); metadata/episodes.parquet lists 2,104 (no Robotiq); paper: 3,215 trials (541 human, 539 Allegro, 743 Inspire F1, 791 Inspire DFTP, 601 Robotiq); GitHub README: 2.1K; HF card: 3.2K.

hours=14.9 derived: catalog num_frames for 2,104 sequences sum to 1,275,339 and Robotiq raw/timestamps/frame_id.npy lengths (568 of 599 sequences) sum to 334,860; 1,610,199 frames / 30 fps = 14.9 h. Excludes ~31 Robotiq sequences without timestamps.
frames=43.5M is the paper's figure and counts images over all camera views.
subjects=1: paper says 'a human subject' / 'A human participant'; not stated as a count. Number of teleoperators not stated.
tasks=1: single grasp-and-lift task type; not a stated count. Paper: 23 of 33 GRASP-taxonomy grasp types.
scene_types=['lab']: one capture platform (21-camera rig around a workspace); no scene count is stated.

Cameras: paper says 21-camera exocentric rig + stereo helmet (human) or static stereo egocentric cameras (robot). In the files the helmet pair is 25452062/25452066 (ego_calib.json has per-frame extrinsics); human and Inspire F1 sequences carry 23 streams, Allegro and Inspire DFTP 22 (no 22684210), Robotiq 22-23 (adds 26256735/26256742, lacks 23029839). Camera models not stated. All streams 2048x1536 mpeg4 tagged 30 fps (metadata/cameras.parquet, one human mp4 probed).
raw/timestamps/timestamp.npy steps median 0.030 s (~33 Hz) in the sampled Allegro, Inspire F1 and DFTP sequences while the mp4 files are tagged 30 fps; Robotiq steps are 0.0333 s.

Tactile and force rates are medians of the time stamps in the sampled files (Allegro hand ~99 Hz, Inspire F1 tactile 50.0 Hz, Inspire DFTP hand ~49.7 Hz). Inspire F1 tangential_direction ranges 0-359 with -1 when unloaded, i.e. likely degrees (not stated). F1 thumb_normal_force reached exactly 3000 in cactus/3 (possible clip).
Inspire DFTP force.npy: values above 32,767 occur and read as small negatives when reinterpreted as int16 (e.g. 65,525 = -11); the channel order (6 actuators) is not documented.
Object pose translations are ~0.3-0.6 in magnitude (consistent with meters; unit not stated). C2R.npy is a 4x4 the official code inverts to get robot_from_world.

Human success labels are null in the catalog (paper: all human trials succeed). Release success counts: Allegro 453/453, Inspire F1 423 true / 164 false / 5 null, Inspire DFTP 387 / 231, Robotiq grasp_result.json 474 / 81 (555 files).

datasets.name: ActionSense
datasets.title: ActionSense: A Multimodal Dataset and Recording Framework for Human Activities Using Wearable Sensors in a Kitchen Environment
datasets.summary: Kitchen activities in a mock kitchen with bimanual 32x32 conductive-thread tactile gloves, Manus bend-sensor finger tracking, Xsens body IMUs, Myo forearm EMG, Pupil Core eye tracking, 5 static RGB cameras and 2 microphones.
datasets.hand: human hands wearing custom open-finger tactile gloves (conductive threads on a piezoresistive film) under Manus Prime II Xsens finger-tracking gloves

sensor.note: One sample per hand = 32x32 matrix of raw ADC readings (float32, 1,024 thread intersections); threads routed to a 23x19 palm grid, 5x9 thumb, 11x4 little finger and 13x4 on each other finger. Open-finger gloves: no fingertips. No matrix-to-hand-location map in the released files.

scale.text: ~13 h recorded (778 min; 543.5 min of activities), 574 labeled activity instances (9 subjects), 20 activities, 10 subjects, 1 mock kitchen; tactile on 6 subjects (S00-S05)

datasets.access: Open HTTP download, no login: per-subject HDF5 (wearables), MP4/AVI (eye-tracking world video), AVI + timestamp TXT (5 RGB cameras) and WAV (microphones) linked from action-sense.csail.mit.edu/data.html; HTTP range requests supported.
caveats: Tactile and finger tracking only for S00-S05; S06-S09 wore no tactile or finger-tracking gloves (their HDF5 files have no tactile-glove groups and only 23 Xsens segments).
S01: wearable data was lost after calibration and peeling cucumbers; its HDF5 holds only calibration plus 3 labeled activities.
Tactile is about 6 Hz in practice (the sensor table on the website lists 15 Hz).

Tactile is raw ADC counts with no conversion to force; the scale calibration periods (Dymo M25 weight_g) are provided for that. Metadata says range [0, 4095], but released values lie in 23..1023 with a ~560 resting baseline.
Tactile response during activities is small: the 20 most-loaded cells typically sit 10-150 counts above baseline.
The HDF5 tactile streams carry no map from the 32x32 matrix to palm/finger regions.
Finger tracking: the data page warns the Manus gloves may not have worked reliably; the Manus IMUs were disabled, so there is no lateral finger spread.
Depth camera data and the external RGB/audio for S06-S09 are listed as 'coming soon' on the data page; raw FLIR frames are not linked (only AVI videos).
Recordings are continuous per subject (1-4 splits); activities are Start/Stop label rows in experiment-activities, not separate files.
Label names vary across subjects (e.g. 'Get items from refrigerator/cabinets/drawers' vs 'Get/replace items ...').

tracking.note: 60 Hz; segment poses, joint angles, CoM, foot contacts; streamed live from MVN, with scripts to merge re-processed MVN estimates
bend sensors, glove IMUs disabled (finger curl only); finger segments arrive through the Xsens stream at 60 Hz (63 segments / 60 joints instead of 23 / 22); site warns finger data may be unreliable
hand segment pose from the body suit; Myo armbands also give forearm orientation (arbitrary reference frame)

other: forearm EMG (Myo armband, 8 ch per arm, ~200 Hz)
eye tracking / gaze and pupil geometry (Pupil Core, ~115 Hz)
Dymo M25 scale weight readings for tactile calibration

sources: https://data.csail.mit.edu/ActionNet/wearable_data/ (all 19 wearable HDF5 files: tree, attributes, rates and tactile values read with HTTP range requests)
unconfirmed: hours = 778.0 min total (includes calibration routines) / 60; activity time alone is 543.5 min (~9.1 h). Tactile streams in the release add up to ~24,570 s (~6.8 h) over the 12 HDF5 files of S00-S05 (left glove time_s spans).

episodes = 574 labeled activity instances over 9 subjects (website activity_stats table, 324.26 min). Pairing Start/Stop rows in the released files gives 586 instances (306 in S00-S05 incl. 3 for S01, 280 in S06-S09) and ~329 min.
frames: tactile frames in the release = 144,404 (left) + 142,048 (right) over S00-S05, counted from the HDF5 tactile_data shapes.
Tactile rate: website sensor table 15 Hz; supplement HDF5 table '6 [improveable to ~15]'; measured 4.5-6.2 Hz per file (time_s), 6.0-6.1 Hz in activity splits.
Egocentric world camera resolution 1280x720 MJPEG, ~29.6 fps: ffprobe of S05 world_frame.mp4 / worldGaze_frame.avi; not stated in the paper.
FLIR AVI videos are MPEG-4 Part 2, 1600x1200, 22 fps (ffprobe of S05 PG1); one timestamp line per frame in the PG*.txt files.

Subjects with tactile: data page says S06-S09 had no gloves; supplement says 'the last 5 subjects'; S01 has tactile only for calibration and 3 activities. The files confirm tactile groups in S00-S05 and none in S06-S09.
taxels_per_hand 682 = 23x19 + 5x9 + 11x4 + 3x(13x4), computed from the stated grids; the file stores all 1,024 matrix intersections.

Released tactile values never exceed 1023 in any of the 12 files although the stream metadata says [0, 4095] (TouchStreamer.py hard-codes that range); how the 32 thread rows/cols map to the hand regions is not documented.
subjects = 10 (data page and supplement); 70% male, 90% right-handed, 27.3 +- 3.7 years.

datasets.name: STAG
datasets.title: Learning the signatures of the human grasp using a scalable tactile glove
datasets.summary: Knitted glove with 548 piezoresistive sensors over the palmar side of the right hand, read as a 32x32 grid at ~7.3 Hz; one subject grasping 26 objects, plus blindfolded, weight and hand-pose sets with synchronized RGB frames.
datasets.hand: human right hand wearing the STAG knitted tactile glove

sensor.note: One sample = a 32x32 int16 map of raw 10-bit ADC counts (0-1023 = 0-5 V amplifier output) from the 32 row x 32 column conductive-thread electrodes; 548 cells are physical sensors, the other 476 are constant. Rest ~510-516, useful signal 500-650, readings over 950 are shorted electrodes. Normal force only.
sensor.range: 30 mN-0.5 N working range per element (responds from ~25 mN, saturates beyond 0.8 N); ~150 quantization levels, ~17.5% peak hysteresis

scale.text: ~6.9 h, 221 recordings, 177,592 tactile frames (135,187 object interaction + 6,686 blindfolded + 11,682 weights + 24,037 hand poses), 26 objects, 1 subject, right hand

datasets.access: Open download (no login) of four zip archives from stag.csail.mit.edu/datasets/, each also as a pressure-only 'lite' zip (49 MB in total).
datasets.license: STAG Research License (research use only, non-commercial, no redistribution)
caveats: License forbids copying or distributing the data other than for your own backup.
Grasping, object identification, weighing and hand-pose articulation, not task-level manipulation.
All recordings are from one person (an author) wearing the glove on the right hand.
Tactile values are raw ADC counts, not calibrated force; the release has no force calibration.
No hand or object tracking; hand-pose classes G1-G7 are labels of articulated poses.
Tactile maps are stored on the 32x32 electrode grid; the sensor-to-hand layout is only embedded in the project's demo pages (sensorIndices/sensorLayout), not in the dataset files.
Camera images were recorded for illustration only and are not used by the authors' code.

other: per-frame preprocessing flags (valid label, balanced, grasp, transition) and train/test split

unconfirmed: hours = 6.9: sum over the 221 recordings of (last ts - first ts) in the four lite metadata.mat files: classification 5.28 h, blindfolded 0.26 h, weights 0.45 h, hand poses 0.92 h. The paper says recordings exceed 5 hours (object set).

episodes = 221 recordings counted in the metadata.mat files: classification 82 (26 objects x 3 days + 4 empty-hand, batches 000/001/002 with 27/27/28), blindfolded 105 (104 identification attempts + 1 empty-hand control), weights 27 (26 objects + empty hand, ~60 s each), hand poses 7 sessions (~452-480 s each, several pose classes per recording).
frames = 177,592: 135,187 + 6,686 + 11,682 + 24,037 frames in the four metadata.mat files; the first and last two match the paper.
tasks = 4 counts the recording protocols (visually aware object interaction, blindfolded identification, weight lift-hold-drop, hand-pose articulation); the paper does not define tasks.
rate_hz = 7.3 is the paper's average frame rate; ts in the files gives a median interval of 0.136 s (7.35 Hz) and a mean of 7.12-7.28 Hz per subset (intervals up to ~0.176 s at p95).

Camera resolution 682x512 is that of the released JPEG frames (fetched from all four archives); the native camera resolution and the camera mount are not stated. The frames show a close view of the gloved hand over a table.

548 valid sensors: exactly 548 of the 1024 grid cells vary in every subset; the other cells are constant 510. The demo page's sensorIndices (32x32, 548 non-negative) matches this mask exactly and sensorLayout gives 2-D hand coordinates per sensor.
Classification values span 446-1000; 51 frames contain a reading above 950 (the paper's shorted-electrode criterion).
scenes not stated; all recordings appear to be on one table surface (from the camera frames).

datasets.name: Tactile textiles
datasets.title: Learning human-environment interactions using conformal tactile textiles
datasets.summary: Machine-knitted piezoresistive glove (722 sensors, 32x32 readout) worn by one person; released glove data is raw pressure maps while holding 27 objects or the bare hand, plus pressing on a digital scale, a tactile vest and a robot-arm sleeve for calibration.
datasets.hand: Knitted tactile glove, one hand (the released calibration code uses the right-glove sensor layout)

datasets.summary: Teleoperated Unitree G1 and H1 humanoids on 246 everyday tasks; the G1 episodes carry Unitree Dex3-1 hand pressure sensors (9 per hand).

sensor.note: G1 episodes only: observation.tactile.values (18, 4) float32 + sensor_id 1-18, NaN-padded to 4. The release's observation.tactile.values (18, 4) is shifted by 13 values: the recording code (GitHub teleop/master.py + worker.py, commit 9611546) writes 13 odometry values and then 216 pressure values (left 9 x 12, then right 9 x 12) but reads the pressure block from where the odometry starts, reshapes to 18 x 12 and keeps indices [0, 2, 9, 11] or [3, 6, 8] per row. Release row k, kept index i is true value p = 12(k-1) + i - 13 (hand p // 108, sensor (p % 108) // 12, element p % 12; p < 0 = odometry), so a release row is not a sensor. After undoing the shift only 22 of the 66 Dex3-1 readings survive (12 left, 10 right); the right hand's palm 2 and 3 fall off the end, the other kept values are 30000 (no reading) or odometry (release row 1 and row 2 col 0). H1/Inspire episodes have empty tactile arrays.

scale.text: Paper: 10.3k trajectories, 260 tasks in 7 categories, 3M+ frames @30 Hz. HF release: 8,949 episodes, 246 tasks, 3,436,171 frames (~31.8 h); tactile G1 part: 4,064 episodes, 124 tasks, ~16.5 h
